3.old: Sardis South is an MLS® sub-area name in the City of Chilliwack. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it.
3.new: Sardis South is a sub-area used in MLS® listings, and the City of Chilliwack hasn’t published a boundary for it.

4.old: As a rough guide, it is the southern part of Sardis around Tyson Road, South Sumas Road and Watson Road, roughly south of Stevenson Road and north of the Vedder neighbourhood. That is an orientation from the addresses of schools, parks and facilities, not a City boundary.
4.new: Roughly speaking, Sardis South is the southern end of Sardis, around Tyson Road, Watson Road and South Sumas Road. Stevenson Road is about its northern edge, and the Vedder neighbourhood lies beyond it to the south. I based this on the addresses of schools, parks and facilities, so treat it as an orientation, not a City boundary.

35.new: Look through MLS listings, prices and area details for homes for sale in Sardis South, Chilliwack, BC, a community near Vedder Road.

100.old: Lot size (FVREB MLS® recorded sales data): the median lot size of detached houses sold in recent 2026 MLS® activity was 6,327 sq ft, based on 30 sales with a recorded lot size.
100.new: From FVREB MLS® recorded sales data on lot size: sold detached houses in the recent 2026 MLS® activity had a median of 6,327 sq ft, drawn from 30 sales where a lot size was recorded.

118.old: The Sardis Neighbourhood Plan covers Sardis, including this area. Council adopted it on January 5, 2021, as OCP Schedule D, through Official Community Plan Amendment Bylaw 2020, No. 5024.
118.new: Sardis South is covered by the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, which Council adopted on January 5, 2021 as OCP Schedule D. The bylaw behind it is No. 5024, the 2020 Official Community Plan Amendment Bylaw.

119.old: The South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan covers the area south of this sub-area. Council adopted it in 2022 and it was updated in 2025 with the Official Community Plan.
119.new: South of Sardis South lies the area covered by the South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan. Council adopted that plan in 2022; an update came in 2025, alongside the Official Community Plan.

120.old: The South Vedder plan area is bordered by the Chilliwack River and Vedder River to the south, the Promontory neighbourhood to the southeast, Tzeachten First Nations Lands to the east, Vedder Road to the west and the Vedder neighbourhood to the north.
120.new: The South Vedder plan area has the Chilliwack River and Vedder River along its south side and the Promontory neighbourhood to its southeast. Tzeachten First Nations Lands lie to the east, Vedder Road marks the west, and the Vedder neighbourhood sits to the north.

121.old: ALR: whether a parcel is in the ALR is set address by address. City-wide, the City says 67% of Chilliwack’s land (17,322 hectares) is in the Agricultural Land Reserve.
121.new: ALR: an individual parcel’s status depends on its address. Across the city as a whole, the City says 17,322 hectares, which is 67% of Chilliwack’s land, lies in the Agricultural Land Reserve.

123.old: The same study says the fan slopes from 36 m elevation near its head to 12 m where it reaches the Fraser floodplain, and that the City’s well field at the head of the fan is the main domestic water supply.
123.new: According to that same study, the fan drops from an elevation of 36 m near its head down to 12 m at the Fraser floodplain, and the City’s well field, located at the head of the fan, serves as the main domestic water supply.

124.old: Floodplain: the City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 designates the floodplains of the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder rivers and the Vedder Canal, plus the alluvial fans and floodplains of several creeks. It sets building setbacks of 75 m from the natural boundary of the Vedder River and 30 m from the Vedder Canal and Chilliwack River.
124.new: In Sardis South, floodplain questions go back to No. 4519, the City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw of 2018. It designates flood-prone land beside the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder rivers, plus the Vedder Canal, and for several creeks it covers the alluvial fans as well as the floodplains. The building setback is 75 m from the Vedder River’s natural boundary and 30 m along the Vedder Canal and the Chilliwack River.

125.old: The City keeps flood response plans for both the Fraser River and the Vedder River, and runs an ongoing $30 million dyke-raising program.
125.new: The City holds flood response plans for the Fraser River and also for the Vedder River, and it is in the middle of a $30 million dyke-raising program.

129.old: If the home is near the Vedder River, Vedder Canal or a creek, ask the City how the floodplain bylaw and its setbacks apply to the exact lot.
129.new: A home near a creek, the Vedder Canal or the Vedder River is worth a call to the City, to find out what the floodplain bylaw and its setbacks mean for that exact lot.

153.old: As a rough guide, it is the southern part of Sardis around Tyson Road, South Sumas Road and Watson Road, roughly south of Stevenson Road and north of the Vedder neighbourhood.
153.new: Sardis South covers the lower part of Sardis near South Sumas Road, Tyson Road and Watson Road, with Stevenson Road to its north and the Vedder neighbourhood to its south, more or less.

154.old: That is an orientation from addresses, not a City boundary, so ask me if a specific address is in it.
154.new: Please ask me whether a particular address falls in it, since this comes from addresses and is not a City boundary.

167.old: The Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, which Council adopted on January 5, 2021, as OCP Schedule D (Bylaw 2020, No. 5024).
167.new: OCP Schedule D, the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, adopted by Council on January 5, 2021 (Bylaw 2020, No. 5024).

170.old: The City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 4519 designates the floodplains of the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder rivers and the Vedder Canal, plus the alluvial fans and floodplains of several creeks. It sets setbacks of 75 m from the Vedder River and 30 m from the Vedder Canal and Chilliwack River.
170.new: Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 4519 is how the City designates floodplains. They run along the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder rivers and by the Vedder Canal, and for several creeks the bylaw names the alluvial fans and the floodplains. Setbacks are 75 m for the Vedder River and 30 m for each of the Vedder Canal and the Chilliwack River.
